entries.content: AS002 is a derived analytical series performing a cross-validation of S506 (Rate of Surplus Value, e = S*/V*) against an alternative computation method attributed to Khanjian. This serves as an internal consistency check for the exploitation rate estimates.
entries.verbatim_quote: Main Formula: (1 + eu) / (1 + ep) ≈ (hu/hp) / (ecu/ecp). Key insight: Relative exploitation rates depend on relative hours and relative compensation.

entries.content: Registry describes AS002 as 'cross-check of S506 vs alternative method' with source_type 'analytical'. The legacy construction script is A08_khanjian_crossvalidation.py. Units are ratio. The series covers 1948-2024.
entries.verbatim_quote: If hu/hp > ecu/ecp → eu > ep (unproductive workers more exploited); If hu/hp < ecu/ecp → eu < ep (productive workers more exploited); If hu/hp = ecu/ecp → eu = ep (equal exploitation).

entries.content: The Khanjian method likely computes the rate of surplus value through an alternative decomposition path — possibly arriving at S*/V* via different intermediate aggregations of the IO accounts. The cross-validation compares this alternative result against the primary S506 series to verify consistency.
entries.verbatim_quote: Table I.1: Rates of Exploitation of Unproductive Workers, 1948-89. Purpose: Annual calculation of eu using 25-step methodology.

entries.content: Key input: S506 (Rate of Surplus Value). The construction array in the registry is empty, indicating this was handled by a standalone analytical script rather than the standard pipeline. Status is book_period_validated, confirming the cross-check passed for the original 1948-1989 period.
entries.verbatim_quote: Hp = H'p - (Hp)t - (Hp)fire. Reason: Authors' productive labor excludes government dummy and FIRE sectors. Example (1948): H'p = 1,379,560; (Hp)t = 40.40 × 8,629 = 348,612 thousand weekly hours; (Hp)fire = 37.90 × 1,496 = 56,698 thousand weekly hours; Hp = 974,250 thousand weekly hours.

entries.content: Khanjian (1989) using consistent procedure: Value and price rates of surplus value differ by only 6%-9%. Price-value deviations have minor effects on aggregate measures (Section 5.10, Table 5.12, Figure 5.25).
entries.context: Ch7 §7.3 | AS002 primary anchor -- this is the book's direct reference to the Khanjian benchmark that AS002 uses as the cross-validation target. Establishes the 6%-9% deviation envelope AS002's cross-check should reproduce.

entries.content: Khanjian's S*/V* uniformly lower than S/V by 6%-9% (Khanjian 1988, p. 109, table 19). Wolff's inconsistent procedure biases money rate S*/V* upward by 12%-15% (sum of two differences).
entries.context: Ch7 §7.3 | AS002 methodology anchor -- contrasts Khanjian's consistent procedure (the reference standard AS002 emulates) against Wolff's biased alternative. Justifies WHY a Khanjian-style cross-validation is the right consistency check rather than a Wolff-style one.

entries.content: Main Formula: (1 + eu) / (1 + ep) approx (hu/hp) / (ecu/ecp). Known: ep = S*/V* (rate of surplus value for productive workers). Solve for eu: eu = (hu/hp) / (ecu/ecp) . [1 + S*/V*] - 1.
entries.context: Appendix I | AS002 derivation anchor -- Appendix I formal derivation of the rate-of-exploitation formula. This is the alternative-decomposition path against which AS002 cross-validates S506 (productive workers' rate of surplus value).

entries.content: Exploitation rate ratio (eu/ep): 1948: 0.80 (unproductive 20% less exploited); 1960: 0.89; 1972: 0.92; 1980: 0.92; 1989: 0.97 (3% less). Convergence: Exploitation rates converging. Both rising, but unproductive rising faster.
entries.context: Appendix I | AS002 validation target -- the headline annual numeric results from Appendix I Table I.1 that AS002's cross-validation must reproduce (eu/ep ratio converging from 0.80 to 0.97 over 1948-1989).
